result.title: Haste Makes Waste? Towards Safe Few-Step Text-to-Image Models
result.summary: While few-step distilled text-to-image models have gained traction due to their fast generation times, the speed-up implications on their unsafe generation rates remain unknown. We uncover an inherent tension between speed and safety: few-step models are often more unsafe than their teachers, and reducing the number of inference steps consistently raises unsafe generation rates. We further find that acceleration makes unsafe concepts harder to erase in few-step models, with existing concept-erasure methods markedly less effective than in teachers. We offer a mechanistic diagnosis for why erasure methods fail on few-step models, finding that the fragility of few-step models' generation process and the way generation guidance is usually distilled into those models may hinder established concept-erasure methods. To address the speed-safety trade-off, we propose DICE (Distillation-Integrated Concept Erasure), a post-distillation erasure method tailored for few-step models. DICE aligns both its latent construction and its generation-preservation loss with the distillation method that produced the model, keeping erasure faithful to few-step models. DICE demonstrates strong results in our evaluation. For example, on FLUX Schnell, DICE reduces unsafe-generation rate to 0.046 (vs. at least 0.161 for prior erasure methods we test), while mostly preserving benign generation quality.

AI.brief_summary: 论文考察少步蒸馏 text-to-image 模型中速度与安全性的张力，指出步数越少不安全事故率越高、概念擦除更难生效，并给出机制诊断，提出与蒸馏方式对齐 latent 构造与生成保持损失的 DICE 擦除方法。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「latent 构造需与产生该模型的蒸馏过程对齐」及少步生成过程脆弱性的诊断，可能为少步/并行生成 latent 推理状态时保真性下降与训练监督对齐提供核查线索，但研究对象是图像生成而非多模态推理。
